critical_rules: The source rubric Corali dall'Autografo di Lipsia is not true collection membership for 13/18 records; BWV 654/658/659/660/661 only are Leipzig Great Eighteen members.
Existing BWV1056 documentary reference in V7 is reused, not cloned as a distinct work identity; document status still not canonical.
BWV1059 is a 9-bar unfinished attempt. Do not claim full no. 8 concerto or generate lost movements.
BWV597 and BWV713a authorship uncertain; BWV733 authorship disputed with Johann Ludwig Krebs proposed; no definitive Bach compone.
BWV594/BWV596 and BWV1065 are Bach transcriptions/arrangements after original works of Antonio Vivaldi RV208, RV565, RV580.
Flaminio misstates opus association for BWV594 Vivaldi RV208 and suggests reversed direction BWV1046-BWV207; record and correct without blindly copying guide.
BWV1046..1051 are six distinct individual concerto works with common documentary collection; do not collapse into one published work and never classify all as concerto grosso automatically.
BWV971 imitates concerto as solo two-manual harpsichord work: no literal orchestra/solo-group edge.
BWV1044 sources are BWV894 movements 1 and 3 and organ-sonata BWV527/2; BWV1054 after BWV1042; BWV1057 after BWV1049; BWV1062 after BWV1043.
Reconstruction of lost original concertos must not be treated as surviving originals; catalogues and genre hierarchy remain staging.
No direct text read is claimed for 24 guides absent from the direct source list, nor independent proof that all 51 identities are globally unique.
